newsitem.title: USA: PaineWebber stock up on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: PaineWebber stock up on takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in PaineWebber Group Inc. rose sharply Friday amid market talk that Morgan Stanley Group Inc. might make a bid for the rival Wall Street firm, analysts said.
The stock rose $3.50 to $34.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on volume of almost 1.5 million shares.
But Morgan Stanley denied the market speculation. "We are not in talks to acquire PaineWebber," a Morgan Stanley spokeswoman said.
A PaineWebber spokesman said it was the company's policy not to comment on the price of its stock, or on rumours or speculation.

Joan Solotar, an industry analyst at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, said Morgan Stanley's flat denial of the rumours, rather than the standard "no comment," is an indication it is truly not interested in acquiring PaineWebber.
"It's not to say (PaineWebber) is not a takeover candidate, but I don't think it's Morgan," Solotar said.
Earlier this month PaineWebber's shares rose sharply after a Business Week article said the brokerage was being eyed as a takeover target by BankAmerica Corp. and others.
Both PaineWebber and BankAmerica declined to comment at the time.
